clue.text: Complain, given part of log for woodwork

parts.note: to carp is to complain or find fault
an entry is one item written in a log or diary

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling while handed a piece of timber for a woodwork class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of log' suggests a chunk of wood, but it is a record entry in a logbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry is the craft of making things from timber, which is what woodwork means.

clue.text: Anglicans receiving fine for illegal substance

indicators.note: receiving says the church letters take the other word inside them

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Churchgoers are fined for possessing drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is slang for cocaine, a banned drug.

clue.text: What priest may don, or bishop tucking into caviar?

explanation.surface: A bishop eating caviar wonders what his priest might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but it puts B inside ROE.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose vestment, the kind of garment clergy wear.

clue.text: Upset setter needs support and hug

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
a brace is a support

explanation.surface: A distressed crossword compiler needs comfort and a cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrace is a hug, holding someone closely in your arms.

clue.text: Tip of tool, item used fencing in American's home

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of tool
an epee is a sword used in the sport of fencing

explanation.surface: A garden worker uses a tool tip and other items to build a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' suggests putting up fences, but it is the sword sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent, the traditional dwelling of some Native American peoples.

clue.text: Delay for a drunk getting large amount of alcohol

indicators.note: drunk, as in disordered, says the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunk person holds things up by ordering a huge drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard of ale is a tall glass holding about two and a half pints of beer, drunk in one go.

clue.text: Like McDonald's food son doesn't eat

definitions.note: a verb phrase in the third person, matching the plural-looking verb form

parts.note: McDonald's sells fast food

explanation.surface: A parent notes that their son refuses to touch burger-chain meals.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end: the verb 'fasts' means goes without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fasts abstains from food, often for religious reasons.

clue.text: Labour leader Michael smiles occasionally in flirtatious activity

parts.note: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: alternate letters of smiles

explanation.surface: A former Labour leader flirts, smiling now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the first, third and fifth letters of 'smiles' gives SIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing footsie is touching someone's feet under a table as a flirtatious gesture.

clue.text: Possible reason for booking limo — aunt is travelling

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone books a limousine because their aunt is going on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is LIMO AUNT IS. 'booking' looks like a reservation, but in football a referee books a player for diving, which is called simulation.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, simulation is faking a foul, and a referee shows a yellow card for it.

clue.text: Dali, say, certainly entertains king and top celebs

indicators.note: entertains means takes in as a guest, so the king goes inside

parts.note: sure means certainly
R is the abbreviation for king, from rex
the A-list is the top rank of celebrities

explanation.surface: The artist Dali is said to host royalty and famous stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Dali as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dali was a leading painter of the Surrealist movement.

clue.text: Dish, starter from Berry in bake off

indicators.note: in says the first letter goes inside the rearranged letters
off, as in gone bad, says the letters of bake are spoiled into a new order
the starter of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of Berry

explanation.surface: A baking-show contestant serves a dish inspired by judge Mary Berry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges BAKE to KEAB, and the B from Berry goes inside it. Mary Berry was a judge on the TV contest The Great British Bake Off.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab is a dish of grilled meat pieces, typically served on a skewer.

clue.text: Theatre backing erstwhile actor, say

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the theatre word is read from its end

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
erstwhile means former, of an earlier time

explanation.surface: A theatre is supporting a has-been actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like financial support for the theatre, but it is the reversal signal. 'say' marks actor as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is one kind of performer, alongside singers, dancers and musicians.

clue.text: Miss album? A demo I sell excitingly covers it

parts.words: album? A demo I sell excitingly
parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musician boasts that their demo album is selling thrillingly well.
explanation.definitionFit: Mademoiselle is the French form of address for an unmarried woman, equivalent to the English title.

clue.text: Camaraderie — working day finishes with it

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday, a working day
ends are finishes
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: Workplace camaraderie as the trendy Friday wraps up.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendship is the bond between friends, the same warm companionship as camaraderie.

clue.text: Foolishly, a cop plays with drug, leading to disaster

indicators.note: foolishly suggests acting in a muddled way, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A policeman plays the fool with drugs, and catastrophe follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening A stays where it is; only COP PLAYS is rearranged, and E (ecstasy) is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocalypse is a catastrophe on a huge scale, the end of the world.

clue.text: Put down iron again

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to suppress or crush, as a revolt
second meaning: ..., press clothes a second time

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning reads the word as RE- plus PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to subdue a feeling or uprising, and re-pressing a shirt is ironing it once more.

clue.text: Dripping is a kind of fat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: soaked through, wet enough to drip
second meaning: ... fat, a type found in animal products

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dripping' is also a kind of fat, beef fat, which tempts a single definition; it is in fact the adjective meaning soaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturated means soaked completely, and saturated fats are a dietary category.

clue.text: President Lincoln not drinking with gangster assisting crime

parts.note: Abe is the usual short name of Abraham Lincoln
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A sober Abraham Lincoln is caught helping a mobster with a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln not drinking' reads as one idea about the president, but each part is a separate piece; TT (teetotal) is the crossword convention for abstaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Abettal is the act of abetting, aiding someone in an offence.

clue.text: Boring implement everybody picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for everybody is taken by its sound

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone grabs a dull tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests dull, but it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Extract Republican found inside bar

indicators.note: found inside says the party letter is placed within the word for bar

parts.note: bar can mean except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: A Republican politician is pulled out of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but here it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short passage taken from a longer text or film.

clue.text: Polish star's point of no return

parts.note: to rub is to polish
an icon is a celebrated person, a star

explanation.surface: A Polish celebrity reaches a turning point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital suggests the nationality, but it is the verb. Caesar crossing the river Rubicon made war inevitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the Rubicon means taking an irrevocable step, from Caesar's march on Rome.

clue.text: Interest Parisian in grand singer called Diana

parts.note: en is French for in
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
Diana Ross is the American singer

explanation.surface: A Parisian is absorbed by a big-name singer called Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross someone is to absorb their attention completely, to interest them deeply.

clue.text: Fawns oddly lost south of wooded area

indicators.note: south of in a down clue places these letters below the wood word

parts.note: a grove is a small wood

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the word

parts.note: odd letters of lost

explanation.surface: Young deer go missing near a patch of woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawns' looks like young deer, but it is the verb meaning flatters servilely.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn and to grovel both mean to behave obsequiously to win favour.

clue.text: Pondering case for discharge and release

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of discharge
liberation means release from captivity

explanation.surface: A prisoner considers the paperwork for their discharge and freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberation is careful thought before a decision, which is what pondering is.

clue.text: Thanks that chap, gathering round lake in America

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so the pronoun holds the round letter

parts.note: he refers to that chap
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Thanking a man who brings everyone together for a drinks round at an American lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe is a large freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada on the California–Nevada border.

clue.text: Italian novelist penning hard copy

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the letter goes inside the name

parts.note: Umberto Eco was the Italian novelist
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An Italian novelist writes out a hard copy of his book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' suggests writing, which suits a novelist, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo repeats a sound, a copy of it; to echo is to imitate.

clue.text: Antelope hasn't finished dash

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope has not completed its sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' looks like a run, but it is the noun meaning flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair and vigour, the same lively style as dash.

clue.text: Husband has whisky after work — it's child's play

indicators.note: after places the whisky word following the earlier letters

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
Scotch is whisky from Scotland

explanation.surface: A husband pours a whisky after his working day, claiming it is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's child's play' looks like a phrase meaning easy, but it is a literal definition: the game is played by children.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a playground game where children hop through squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: Swimmer, about 90, is to show great skill

parts.note: an eel is a fish, a swimmer
XC is 90 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A swimmer of about ninety is still remarkably skilful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about 90' reads as an approximate age, but 'about' is the containment signal and 90 is a Roman numeral.

clue.text: Section of prenup re-energised groom

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like the man in the wedding, but it is the verb meaning to tidy oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To preen is to groom oneself, as a bird tidies its feathers.

clue.text: Put on casual clothes and wig

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to wear informal clothes
second meaning: to wig is to scold

explanation.walkthrough: 'wig' looks like a hairpiece, but it is an old British verb meaning to rebuke.
